key_insight: The paper demonstrates an arbitrary-phase controlled-Z entangling gate between two spatially separated superconducting nodes using a traveling microwave photon whose reflected phase depends on the remote qubit state.
engineering_relevance: This enables distributed quantum-network operations such as remote readout and inter-node entanglement without requiring tight synchronization of the distant node.
method: Connect two dilution cryostats with a 30-meter cryogenic quantum link.
Send a microwave photon from node A to node B and vary its frequency to tune the conditional reflection phase.
Use the resulting photon-state interaction to implement remote single-shot readout of qubit B from node A.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a realized bidirectional photon-transfer experiment across the two-node circuit QED link, with the entangling operation used to perform single-shot remote readout.
watch_item: The approach depends on maintaining high-fidelity photon transfer and phase control over a long cryogenic link, which may be sensitive to loss, dispersion, and calibration drift.
paper_title: Arbitrary-phase CZ gate and remote readout across spatially separated superconducting nodes
